clue.text: A place in Spain

parts.note: read as the Spanish word for a town's public square, the clue's 'place' taken in the sense of the French place or a square

explanation.definitionFit: In Spanish towns the open public square, the equivalent of a French place, goes by this name.

clue.text: Physical education contest arranged for the feast

parts.note: PE is the usual abbreviation for physical education, the school gym lesson

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the word contest are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A school sports contest is organised for a church festival day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' signals the anagram; 'the feast' is a church festival, Whitsun.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitsun, the church festival seven weeks after Easter, is a feast day of the Christian calendar.

clue.text: Skill embracing success in common parlance

indicators.note: embracing means the first word holds the second within its arms

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation
a go is a success, as in making a go of it

explanation.surface: Someone with a gift for talking makes a hit in everyday speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' signals the container; 'success' as in making a go of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang or jargon of a particular group is everyday speech of a sort, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Pope's great queen receives X with this aerial

indicators.note: receives means the queen's name takes the number into its middle

parts.note: Alexander Pope addressed Queen Anne as 'great Anna' in The Rape of the Lock
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A queen in a poem gets a mysterious X along with a radio mast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receives' signals the container. The queen comes from Pope's line 'Here thou, great Anna! whom three realms obey'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod or wire picking up radio signals is called both an aerial and by this word.

clue.text: Gilbertian baby-farmer found in a meadow

definitions.meaning: Little ___ in Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore admits she once took in infants for money and mixed two babies up
a yellow wild flower common in grassland

explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert's bumboat woman in HMS Pinafore bears the name of the yellow meadow flower.

clue.text: Being an eager worker is old hat

definitions.meaning: from the phrase eager ___, a keen hard worker, after the busy dam-building animal
an old-fashioned top hat made of the animal's fur

explanation.definitionFit: The industrious rodent gives both the phrase for a keen toiler and the name of a fur top hat once worn.

clue.text: Tea, some say, should suffice such a type

definitions.text: Tea, some say, should suffice such a type

parts.words: Tea, some say, should suffice such a type
parts.note: describes someone for whom tea alone will do, with a nod to the popular story that the word for abstaining began as 'tea total'

explanation.definitionFit: A person who abstains from alcohol makes do with non-alcoholic drinks such as tea.

clue.text: Text so improved when concluded without the first person

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for finished goes round the pronoun

parts.note: concluded means finished, over
me is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A piece of writing gets better once the author is cut out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so the first person is wrapped rather than removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A text that has been corrected and revised by an editor is said to be improved in this way.

clue.text: This sort of ship is not in race for conversion

indicators.note: for conversion means the words not in race are to be changed into something else

explanation.surface: A vessel is not entered in the regatta because it is being refitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Vessels built to carry cargo in standard steel boxes are named after those boxes.

clue.text: A bit of tranquillity for listeners

indicators.note: for listeners means the word for calm is judged by how it is heard, not how it is spelt

parts.note: tranquillity is peace and quiet

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a little calm so people can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for listeners' signals that PEACE gives a word said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment or portion of something is a synonym for a bit.

clue.text: Man on board chief magistrate said is an incubus

indicators.note: said means the two pieces are heard spoken aloud rather than read as spelt

parts.note: a knight is a chessman, a man on the board, and a mayor is a town's chief magistrate

explanation.surface: A chess piece and a town's leading official are called a demon.
explanation.walkthrough: KNIGHT and MAYOR spoken together sound like the answer; 'said' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus, originally a demon thought to sit on sleepers, came to mean an oppressive bad dream.

clue.text: He picks winners, including one in Sea Eagle

indicators.note: including means the bird's name takes the numeral within it

parts.note: the erne is the white-tailed sea eagle
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A racing tipster backs one horse called Sea Eagle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts I into ERNE before its last letter. The British Premium Bond prize draw is made by a machine with this acronym name.
explanation.definitionFit: The random number generator that selects Premium Bond prize numbers is known by this name, so it chooses the winners.

clue.text: Smith Minor's drink in a marquee creating this international bonhomie?

definitions.text: Smith Minor's drink in a marquee creating this international bonhomie?

parts.words: Smith Minor's drink in a marquee creating this international bonhomie?
parts.note: a schoolboy's version of French: a fruit cordial drunk 'en tente', in a tent, punning on the name of the 1904 Anglo-French understanding

explanation.definitionFit: The friendly understanding between Britain and France agreed in 1904 is known by this French phrase meaning cordial agreement.

clue.text: Examination of French form included a severe test

indicators.note: included means the French word sits within the word for the test

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
de is the French form of the word of

explanation.surface: A French exam was part of a harsh trial for the pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' signals the container; 'of French form' is the French word for of.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial by fire or water in old law, or any painful experience, is a hard test of endurance.

clue.text: Fashion in which the cloth takes the lead?

definitions.text: Fashion in which the cloth takes the lead?

parts.words: Fashion in which the cloth takes the lead?
parts.note: the cloth means the clergy, and the lead is what one attaches to a pet's neckwear

explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman's stiff white band at the neck shares its name with the strap a pet wears to take a lead.

clue.text: I'd scorn a revised version with such laughter

definitions.note: the definition describes laughter of the kind meant, so it stands for an adjective

indicators.note: a revised version means the letters of I'd scorn a are rewritten in another order

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a rewritten edition and laughs bitterly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a revised version' rearranges I'D SCORN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking, cynical laughter is described with this adjective, from a Greek word for bitter scornful laughter.

clue.text: Type a letter

definitions.meaning: a type is a person of a particular kind, as in quite a figure
a single written symbol, as in Chinese script

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a distinctive person and a written symbol such as a letter of an alphabet.

clue.text: Guy comes on small wood of swampy growth

indicators.note: comes on means the first word comes before the other, on top of it in a down entry

parts.note: a guy is a man
a grove is a small wood or group of trees

explanation.surface: A fellow arrives at a little copse of marshy vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical trees growing in coastal swamps and tidal mud are known by this name.

clue.text: Though fast with a roll of notes, he's very stingy

definitions.note: the definition describes the person, standing for a noun meaning a miser

parts.note: tight means fast, firmly fixed
a wad is a roll of banknotes

explanation.surface: Though a man has plenty of cash in his pocket he will not spend it.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser or skinflint is called this in informal American usage.

clue.text: Farming up to one's declining years?

parts.note: till means up to, until
age as in old age, one's later years

explanation.surface: Working the land until one grows old.
explanation.definitionFit: Cultivating and ploughing land is a part of agriculture.

clue.text: A gin's knocked back here in Greece

indicators.note: knocked back means the whole phrase is read backwards, while suggesting a drink downed

parts.note: a gin is a trap for animals, so gins or gin's gives traps

explanation.surface: Someone downs a gin while on holiday in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns A TRAPS into the answer. The surface wants gin to be the drink; it is the animal trap.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient city-state famed for its warriors lies in the southern Peloponnese of Greece.

clue.text: A doggedly progressive type Gray's ploughman

definitions.meaning: someone who makes slow steady progress by persistent effort
in Thomas Gray's Elegy the ploughman 'homeward plods his weary way'

explanation.definitionFit: A slow, persistent worker trudges on, as Gray's ploughman trudges homeward.

clue.text: Milton's mother of arts, a bird in wartime service

indicators.note: in means the bird is placed inside the abbreviation

parts.note: the ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the British women's army branch in World War Two
a hen is a bird

explanation.surface: Milton's mother of the arts was a girl serving in the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. Milton calls the Greek capital 'mother of arts' in Paradise Regained; the 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's Paradise Regained praises the Greek capital as the eye of Greece and the source of learning and the arts.

clue.text: Almost nothing composed about love — a musical work

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the letter for love
composed means the letters of almost nothing are arranged afresh, as music is

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Barely anything was written about love in a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' suggests music but signals the anagram, and 'about' wraps the anagram round the letter for love.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Piano Sonata No 14 is popularly known by this name, so it is a musical work.

clue.text: Complaint that goes begging, it was said

definitions.meaning: a complaint is an illness, here the infectious swelling of the glands

definitions.text: that goes begging, it was said
definitions.meaning: to mump was an old word for to beg

explanation.definitionFit: The disease of swollen salivary glands, and an archaic verb meaning to go about begging, share the same letters.

clue.text: A tie-up with a judicial decision

parts.note: ward means custody or confinement, a tying up, as in being held in ward

explanation.surface: A link-up comes with a ruling from the court.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbitrator's or court's settlement of a dispute is a judicial ruling.

clue.text: More than one' cross this island boasts

definitions.text: More than one' cross this island boasts

parts.words: More than one' cross this island boasts
parts.note: the island has both the eight-pointed cross of its Knights and the George Cross awarded to it in 1942

explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean island gave its name to the Knights' eight-pointed cross and holds the George Cross.

clue.text: Concerning the sort of beer, say, enjoyed in Queer Street

definitions.note: Queer Street is old British slang for being in debt, so this is what a person in debt has

parts.note: over means concerning, as in arguing over money

indicators.note: say means the beer word is heard spoken and gives a word that sounds the same

parts.note: draught beer is drawn from a cask

explanation.surface: Discussing which beer to drink while broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns DRAUGHT into DRAFT, said the same way. Queer Street is British slang for money trouble; 'enjoyed' is ironic.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank debt drawn beyond what the account holds is the mark of someone short of money.

clue.text: Circe, for one, or the corn. goddess on board

annotationWithheld.why: Circe, for one, or the corn. goddess on board (9): the only parse is OR CERES inside SS, where 'on board' both gives SS (steamship) and signals the insertion, one phrase doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Circe, for one, or the corn. goddess on board

clue.text: Fliers thereby detected going West to East or vice versa

indicators.text: going West to East or vice versa
indicators.note: going either way across the entry means the word reads the same left to right and right to left

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Aircraft are spotted flying east or west.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads the same in both directions, which is all the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft are located by the radio echoes of this detection system.
